text.content:
- Biggest single lever for retention: instead of a user re-searching manually, re-run their saved search on a schedule and Telegram-notify them of new matches (telegram-bot infra already exists).
- NEEDS LOK'S CALL, not building blind: requires standing scheduled compute (this app is currently pure static export + on-demand edge functions, no cron), and every scheduled re-run spends real Tavily/Gemini quota whether or not a user is looking - directly conflicts with the tight shared 1,000/month budget unless scoped carefully (e.g. daily cap, opt-in per search, dedupe against what has already been shown).

--- SCOPING PROPOSAL (1pm session, 27.08.2026) - for Lok to approve or adjust at the 6pm report ---
- Blocker today: saved searches are localStorage-only (per browser), so no backend can see them to re-run. And the Telegram bot currently only sends to Lok's own hardcoded chat_id - there is no multi-user wiring.
- Proposed MVP (about one session to build once approved):
  1. New Supabase table saved_searches: id (opaque token), query_text, filters_json, telegram_chat_id, last_seen_urls (text[]), created_at, last_notified_at. This would be the app's first shared/server-side data - everything today is stateless + localStorage.
  2. Onboarding with no accounts: an "Alert me" button on a search opens a Telegram deep link (t.me/<bot>?start=<token>); the bot captures that user's chat_id and links it to the row. No passwords, no login.
  3. New edge function alerts: for one saved_searches row, re-runs the existing search pipeline, diffs results against last_seen_urls, Telegrams only the genuinely-new listings, then updates last_seen_urls.
  4. Cron: GitHub Actions schedule: (free, same runner that already deploys the site) calls alerts once per day.

• Verified: 1 live search call still returns listings correctly post-refactor, plus free validation-path checks on verdict/tutorial/parts all still 400 correctly. Deployed all 4 functions.

Board was dry (both remaining items blocked on Lok's product calls), so did another code audit. Found: all 3 Supabase functions (search/verdict/tutorial) called await req.json() directly with no try/catch - same crash class as the JSON.parse-on-Gemini-response bug fixed earlier today. A malformed/empty request body would throw uncaught, producing a 500 with no CORS headers instead of the friendly error every other failure path returns. Low real-world likelihood (the frontend always sends valid JSON) but genuinely reachable by any non-browser client hitting the endpoint directly, and it's the same fix pattern already applied elsewhere in these files, so applied it uniformly for consistency.

Fix: wrapped req.json() in try/catch, returns a 400 with the existing corsHeaders on failure, same shape as the adjacent validation checks.

Verified live with a raw curl POST of invalid JSON to the search function: now returns a clean 400 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin present, instead of crashing. Zero Tavily/Gemini calls spent on this - build clean, all 3 functions redeployed, pushed.

Root cause: the search bar wrapper is flex flex-col (mobile) / sm:flex-row (desktop+); flex-1 only controls width in row-direction, so in the mobile flex-col state the <input> fell back to its browser-default intrinsic width (~200px) instead of filling the screen, leaving a large dead area. Likely present on every mobile view before this fix, not something introduced today. Fix: added w-full to the input and button (button also gets sm:w-auto so it stays compact once inline at desktop width). Verified via DOM measurement (getBoundingClientRect) that the input now correctly spans the available width at 380px - the Browser pane's own screenshot tool had an unrelated width-capture quirk that made this hard to confirm visually, DOM measurement was the reliable check. Deployed and live.
